title: When the Cipher Sings
premise: Felix Marchetti, a night-shift dispatcher who has quietly untangled three 'accidental' deaths from the patterns of his radio log, receives two letters in one envelope: a confession to a murder no one reported, and a promise that more will follow unless he finds Marisol Vega, a witness officially declared dead seven years ago. As Felix follows the cipher hidden in old dispatch records, he discovers his own late father helped falsify Marisol's death for the Calder family, whose shipping empire is built on that buried crime. The letters are coming from inside the taxi company itself, and each death Felix failed to prevent was someone who got close to the truth. In the end, Felix must choose between exposing the inheritance that protects everyone he works with—including the dispatcher who trained him—and delivering Marisol, alive and hiding in plain sight as the company's archivist, to the people who will kill to keep her dead on paper.
about_author: Paloma Okafor is a former emergency-services dispatcher who spent six years listening to a city breathe through a headset before turning those nights into fiction. She writes mysteries about ordinary people who notice too much, and lives near a harbor where she claims the fog still keeps secrets.

chapters.title: The Quiet Hours
chapters.summary: POV Felix. A slow night shift at Meridian Taxi's dispatch desk establishes Felix's ritual: logging anomalies no one else sees, including the cab route that contradicts the official story of a dockworker's fatal fall. He's careful, invisible, content to solve deaths on paper and tell no one. Emotional beat: lonely competence—the comfort of being unseen.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes, One Hand
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Twin letters arrive with his pay stub: one confesses to the dockworker's murder in precise detail; the other promises a fourth death unless Felix locates Marisol Vega, a witness declared dead in 2017. The handwriting matches his father's old dispatch annotations. Emotional beat: dread cracking open routine—the invisible man has been seen.

chapters.title: What the Log Remembers
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Pulling archived dispatch tapes, Felix maps the three 'accidents' against cab routes and realizes each victim had requested a ride to the same address the night they died. His mentor, senior dispatcher Ruth Calloway, catches him in the archive and warns him off with genuine fear. Emotional beat: the thrill of pattern curdling into isolation.

chapters.title: The Calder Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV alternating Felix and a brief interlude from Ruth. Felix researches the Vega family's drowned cargo claim against Calder Shipping and learns his late father co-signed the paperwork declaring Marisol dead. Ruth's interlude reveals she knows more than she's said and is reporting to someone. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden—his father's silence becomes his own.

chapters.title: Fourth Fare
chapters.summary: POV Felix. The promised fourth death arrives: a retired mechanic who once serviced the Calder fleet dies in a garage fire ruled accidental. Felix arrives before police and finds the same route anomaly burned into the work order. For the first time he reports what he knows—to Detective Ibarra, who once dismissed him. Emotional beat: guilt made active; invisibility starts costing lives.

chapters.title: Dead Woman Working
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Following payroll irregularities, Felix discovers the company archivist, 'Mara Voss,' is Marisol Vega—alive, hidden by his father's forgery, protected by Ruth. Marisol refuses to testify: the Calders hold her brother's debts and her survival depends on staying legally dead. Emotional beat: the witness found, but truth and mercy pull apart.

chapters.title: The Confessor's Voice
chapters.summary: POV Felix with a recorded-letter interlude. A third letter contains a voice recording; Felix recognizes the cadence as Ruth's son Danny, a former dispatcher who left after the first accident. The confessor and the threatener are different hands using the same penmanship lessons. Emotional beat: betrayal reframed—Ruth has been protecting her son, not the Calders.

chapters.title: Night of the Open Line
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Danny, cornered by the Calders' fixer, takes over the dispatch frequency and broadcasts the whole conspiracy across every cab radio, forcing Felix to choose: shut him down and preserve the fragile plan, or let the city hear everything. The fixer traces the broadcast to the depot. Emotional beat: climax of loyalty vs. truth—silence as complicity.

chapters.title: What Survives the Fire
chapters.summary: POV Felix. Confrontation at the depot: the fixer comes for Danny and Marisol; Ruth takes a bullet shielding her son; Felix uses the dispatch system itself—routing cabs, sirens, and Ibarra's waiting team—to trap the killer mid-escape. The Calders' heir is arrested when the forged death certificate surfaces. Emotional beat: chaos turned into instrument; the quiet skill saves them.

chapters.title: Signing Off
chapters.summary: POV Felix, epilogue weeks later. Marisol testifies under her real name; Danny surrenders to face manslaughter charges; Ruth recovers but retires. Felix declines promotion, stays on nights, and mails one last letter—an honest confession of everything he saw and never reported—to Ibarra. Emotional beat: resolution through chosen visibility; the price of survival finally paid in full.
